results.title: Constitutional protection of national security/a study in light of the ...
results.content: In Jordan, the Council of Ministers, as the body with general jurisdiction over the management of all internal and external affairs of the state, plays a central and essential role in formulating policies and making decisions that protect national security (Jordanian Constitution, 1952, Art 45). On the other hand, the National Security Council, as a constitutional body established under the 2022 constitutional amendments, is also tasked with handling the state’s higher affairs related to security, defense, and foreign policy, with the aim of confronting internal and external challenges represented by the threats of terrorism, conflicts and disputes and others (Jordanian Constitution, 1952, Art 122). Finally, it can be said that the Jordanian Constitution refers to the competencies and powers of the National Security Council in a brief and general manner in Article (122/2), merely stating them in four words under the broad description of *‘*Higher affairs*’* namely, security, defense, and foreign policy.
